sources.title: AGENTS.md: persistent project instructions
sources.note: Author's guide: AGENTS.md should stay short because it is guidance, not enforced configuration, so controls belong in permissions or sandboxing.

sources.title: Context engineering for agents
sources.note: Author's guide: load only what the current decision needs and keep the rest on demand; it cites one external article.

sources.title: Hooks: checks that run on their own
sources.note: Author's guide: hooks guarantee steps that must happen every time, where a written instruction can be skipped; it cites the Claude Code hooks docs.

sources.title: Safe agent execution
sources.note: Author's guide: written instructions cannot reliably stop an agent, so safety should come from layered permissions, sandboxing and approvals in the environment.

sources.title: Piece: security
sources.note: Author's harness template with permission rules and a PreToolUse hook that guard secrets and irreversible commands; its README says none of it is a sandbox and that each agent's own settings must point to the hooks and permissions, so they are wired by hand.

sources.title: Skills: reusable procedures for agents
sources.note: Author's guide: a skill loads only when needed, and its description decides when that happens; it cites the Claude Code skills docs.

sources.title: Tools and permissions
sources.note: Author's guide: the host decides whether a tool call runs, so allow, ask and block rules belong in configuration rather than in the prompt.

sources.title: Verification and evaluation
sources.note: Author's guide: check an agent's claim of completion with runnable tests, type checks and linters rather than trusting its own report.

sources.title: Best practices for Claude Code
sources.note: Says to give Claude a check it can run, such as tests, a build, a linter or a screenshot, so it can verify its own changes.

sources.title: Explore the .claude directory
sources.note: Session transcripts in ~/.claude are plaintext and keep what tools read, such as .env values, until cleanupPeriodDays removes them.

sources.title: Hooks reference
sources.note: Documents PreToolUse hooks that block a tool call with exit code 2 or a deny decision; says a failing hook lets the action proceed unless onFailure is block (Claude Code v2.1.295 or later), and that the if filter is best-effort, so permission rules are the hard control.

sources.title: Hooks reference: hook events
sources.note: Lists the hook events, where PostToolUse runs after a tool call succeeds and cannot stop it, and PreToolUse can block the call.

sources.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
sources.note: Covers project-scoped servers in .mcp.json, which need approval in interactive sessions, and warns to verify trust in each server and about prompt injection.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: sharing AGENTS.md through an import
sources.note: Says a CLAUDE.md can import AGENTS.md with an @AGENTS.md line so both tools read one file, and that the import never makes Claude read AGENTS.md twice.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: choosing which instruction files load
sources.note: Says the setting that changes which instruction files load is read from user, command-line or managed settings and ignored in project and local settings files; the default is to read CLAUDE.md files, or AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md exists above the working directory.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: importing files
sources.note: Says @path imports are expanded and loaded at launch with the file that imports them, so they organize a long file without reducing its context cost.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: what loads at session start
sources.note: Says a user CLAUDE.md in ~/.claude applies to every project, user-level rules load too, rules without paths load at launch while path-scoped rules load only with matching files, and the first 200 lines or 25 KB of auto memory load at the start of every conversation.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: how CLAUDE.md files load
sources.note: Says CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files from the working directory and every directory above it load at launch, and that files in subdirectories load once Claude reads, writes or edits a file there.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: keeping instructions consistent
sources.note: Says contradictory instructions may be followed arbitrarily, asks for periodic review of outdated or conflicting files, and describes a prompt audit that flags references to files or commands that do not exist.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project
sources.note: States that CLAUDE.md and auto memory are context, not enforced configuration (a PreToolUse hook blocks an action); more specific, concise instructions are followed more consistently; keep each CLAUDE.md under 200 lines because longer files cost context and reduce adherence.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project: AGENTS.md
sources.note: Says Claude reads AGENTS.md by default only when no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or above it.

sources.title: Choose a permission mode
sources.note: Lists the permission modes and what each runs without asking; says project settings ignore auto and bypassPermissions, that acceptEdits approves mkdir, touch, rm, rmdir, mv, cp and sed inside the working directory, and that deny rules apply in every mode, including bypassPermissions.

sources.title: Choose a permission mode: boundaries you state in conversation
sources.note: Says auto mode's classifier treats boundaries stated in the conversation as a block signal, that they are not stored as rules and can be lost when context is compacted, and that a deny rule is the hard guarantee.

sources.title: Choose a permission mode: critical paths
sources.note: Says rm and rmdir on the filesystem root, the home directory or the working directory are never approved by an allow rule or an allow hook, and that a matching deny rule still blocks them.

sources.title: Choose a permission mode: protected paths
sources.note: Lists directories and files such as .git, .claude and .mcp.json whose writes are not auto-approved outside bypassPermissions, and says allow rules in settings files do not pre-approve those writes.

sources.title: Configure permissions
sources.note: Rules are checked deny first, then ask, then allow; a Read or Edit deny covers the file tools, recognized Bash file commands such as cat and tee, and Bash redirection targets, and a Read deny also blocks Edit and Write on the same path, but not commands that read files without naming them or scripts that open files themselves; Bash rules are not a security boundary around the program.

sources.title: Configure the sandboxed Bash tool
sources.note: The sandbox is off by default, covers shell commands but not file tools, MCP or hooks, and runs on macOS, Linux and WSL2 but not on native Windows.

sources.title: Security
sources.note: Lists Claude Code's built-in protections (permission modes, sandboxed Bash, Accept Edits, prompt-injection safeguards); says the working-directory boundary is a permission prompt, so an approved Bash command can still write anywhere the user can; and says no system is completely immune to attacks.

sources.title: Settings files and precedence
sources.note: Explains the settings scopes (managed, command line, project local, shared project, user) and which value wins when a key such as permissions or hooks is set in several.

sources.title: Extend Claude with skills
sources.note: Skill descriptions stay in context while the full SKILL.md loads only when invoked, and the skill listing truncates a description at 1,536 characters.

sources.title: Create custom subagents
sources.note: Subagents are Markdown files with frontmatter that run with their own tools; when the main conversation runs in acceptEdits, auto or bypassPermissions, the subagent runs in that mode and ignores its own permissionMode field.

sources.title: Tools reference
sources.note: Lists the built-in tools with their permission requirements, and says Bash output stays inline up to about 30,000 characters by default before it is saved to a file.

sources.title: Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?
sources.note: Its abstract reports that repository context files do not generally raise coding agents' task success and raise inference cost by more than 20% on average.

sources.title: AI Copilot Code Quality: 2025 Look Back at 12 Months of Data
sources.note: Vendor data report from GitClear, not peer reviewed: it finds a rise in copy-pasted and cloned lines in code changes from 2020 to 2024.

sources.title: Coding on Copilot: 2023 Data Suggests Downward Pressure on Code Quality
sources.note: Vendor data report from GitClear, not peer reviewed: it finds copy-pasted code rising relative to moved code in changes from 2020 to 2023.

sources.title: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
sources.note: Describes the risk of LLM systems given too many tools, permissions or autonomy, and recommends least-privilege tools and human approval for high-impact actions.

sources.title: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure
sources.note: Describes LLM applications leaking sensitive data such as credentials and personal data, and recommends sanitizing data and applying least privilege.

sources.title: 2025 Top 10 Risk & Mitigations for LLMs and Gen AI Apps
sources.note: OWASP's 2025 list of the ten main risks for LLM applications, including excessive agency and sensitive information disclosure.

sources.title: Ponytail
sources.note: A skill (skills/ponytail/SKILL.md) with a six-step decision ladder: does it need to exist, is it already in the codebase, standard library or platform, installed dependency, one line, minimal code; its benchmark figures (39 tasks, 5 runs) are the author's claims, not verified.
